title: Preparation of single cell suspensions enriched in mouse brain vascular cells for single-cell RNA sequencing
protocol: Anesthetize a mouse with isoflurane.
Conduct a trans-cardial perfusion using ice-cold DPBS.
Collect brain tissue in ice-cold HBSS.
Prepare enzyme mix 1.
Warm enzyme mix 1 at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Dissect out cortical tissue on a 100 mm petri dish.
Remove the cerebellum from the mouse brain.
Halve the cerebrum along the longitudinal fissure and dissect out the subcortex, hippocampus, and midbrain.
Dissect the cortex for downstream neural cell dissociation and isolation of vascular enriched cells.
Cut brain tissue into small pieces using surgical scissors in enzyme mix 1.
Pass the brain chunks through a Pasteur pipet to ensure consistency of the initial brain mince.
Add enzyme mix 2 to further dissociate the cortex, resulting in a cloudy suspension.
Pass the brain suspension through a 20 G and 23 G needle to generate a homogeneous cell suspension with a murky smooth consistency.
Set up the Quadro MACS Separator for processing.
Add 2925 μL of enzyme mix 1 into a 5 mL snap cap Eppendorf tube.
Move brain cortices into the 0.5 mL tube containing enzyme mix 1, removing excess HBSS.
Cut the brain tissue into small pieces with sharp dissection scissors until small enough to pass through the opening of a Pasteur pipet (approximately 30 seconds).
Incubate samples for 17 minutes at 37°C under continuous rotation at 20 rpm using a rotator.
Prepare enzyme mix 2 at room temperature (RT; 20°C–26°C) during the incubation period.
After incubation, remove the tube from the laboratory oven and add 45 μL of enzyme mix 2 per sample.
Mix the tissue/enzyme solution 10–15 times at a rate of 1 mL/s using a sterilized glass cotton-plugged Pasteur pipet topped with a rubber bulb.
Tap the bottom of the tube if a larger piece of tissue gets stuck to the pipet tip.
Incubate samples for 12 min at 37°C under continuous rotation at 20 rpm.
Pass the tissue/enzyme solution 5 times using a 1 mL syringe with a 20 G needle at a rate of 0.5 mL/s.
Switch to a 1 mL syringe with a 23 G needle and pass the tissue/enzyme solution 10 times at a rate of 0.25 mL/s until solid pieces are no longer visible.
Incubate samples for 10 min at 37°C under continuous rotation at 20 rpm.
Rinse a 70 μm cell strainer with 2 mL of ice-cold calcium and magnesium free DPBS.
Transfer the tissue/enzyme solution to a 50 mL conical tube and add 20 mL ice-cold DPBS.
Apply the tissue suspension to the 70 μm cell strainer placed on a separate 50 mL collection tube on ice.
Centrifuge the tissue suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant carefully and completely.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1,800 μL of cold MACS buffer (4°C).
Add 200 μL of Myelin Removal Beads to the resuspended cells.
Mix well.
Incubate for 15 min at 37°C without rotation.
After incubation, add 18 mL of cold MACS buffer.
Centrifuge the mixture at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL MACS buffer.
Place 15 mL conical collection tubes below each column.
Rinse three LS columns per sample with 3 mL of MACS buffer.
Apply 1 mL of cell suspension to each LS column.
Wash the column twice with 1 mL of MACS buffer.
Collect the total effluent from the columns.
Combine eluents from the 3 separate columns of the same sample.
Centrifuge the eluent at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Mix 0.5 mL of 10× Red Blood Cell Lysis Solution with 4.5 mL ddH2O to prepare a 1× solution.
Keep the 1× Red Blood Cell Lysis Solution at room temperature (RT).
Aspirate the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of ice-cold MACS buffer.
Add 5 mL of 1× Red Blood Cell Lysis Solution to the cell suspension.
Vortex gently for 5 seconds, avoiding settings above 600 rpm.
Incubate at RT for 2 minutes.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant after incubation.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 90 μL of MACS buffer.
Add 10 μL of CD11b MicroBeads to the resuspended cells.
Incubate for 15 minutes in a 4°C refrigerator, not on ice.
Aspirate the supernatant after incubation.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 500 μL of MACS buffer.
Apply the cell suspension to the MS column.
Wash columns three times with 500 μL of MACS buffer.
Collect total effluent.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Prepare 1X Binding buffer by adding 4.75 mL ddH2O to 0.25 mL of 20X Binding Buffer Stock Solution per sample.
Keep on ice.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 100 μL of Dead Cell Removal MicroBeads.
Incubate for 15 min at RT.
Rinse 1 MS column per sample with 500 μL of 1× Binding buffer.
Add 1 mL of 1× Binding buffer to the cell/bead suspension.
Apply the cell suspension to the MS column.
Wash the column four times with 500 μL of 1× Binding buffer.
Collect everything.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of cell suspension solution (0.04% BSA).
Take 10 μL of the cell suspension and mix thoroughly with 10 μL of trypan blue.
Load 10 μL of the mixture onto a disposable hemacytometer.
Determine the cell viability using a bright-field microscope.
Centrifuge the cell pellet at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the cell suspension solution.
Adjust the cell suspension to approximately 1×10^6 cells/mL of live cells.
Load approximately 3,000 gliovascular cells per animal into each sample well according to the 10× Chromium Controller protocol (10× Genomics).
Freeze surplus cells as cell pellet or in appropriate buffer for RNA extraction at -80°C for future real-time PCR experiments.
Prepare libraries for scRNA-Seq using Chromium™ Single Cell 3′ Library & Gel Bead Kit v2.
Construct single cell libraries according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Sequence the libraries at the 3′ end by an Illumina HiSeq 4000 Sequencing System.
Ensure sequencing is conducted at an average depth of 60,000 reads per cell.
